newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OLYMPICS-CAPE TOWN JUBILANT AT 2004 SHORTLISTING.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-CAPE TOWN JUBILANT AT 2004 SHORTLISTING.

text.p: Sports officials and politicians in Cape Town were overjoyed on Friday at the city's selection for the shortlist of possible venues for the 2004 Summer Olympic Games.

President Nelson Mandela said in a statement the International Olympic Committee (IOC) decision to include Cape Town on the shorltist of five candidates was an outstanding achievement for South Africa and the continent.
"It is a validation of our capabilities and an expression of confidence in Africa as a continent with a bright future," Mandela said in a statement.
"The prospect of an Olympic Games in Cape Town presents South Africa with yet another challenge to play an active role in the African Renaissance," he added.
Several thousand people leaped to their feet and screamed with joy as the city's name was announced on a public service radio broadcast at the Waterfront, Cape Town's premier tourist venue.
Their cheers drowned out the names of Rome and Stockholm which followed in alphabetical order.
Five little girls released white pigeons and thousands of balloons in the colours of the South African flag and the bid logo.
Hundreds of supporters had been holding crossed fingers in the air as they waited for the names to be broadcast from Lausanne.
Local politicians hugged each other and the crowd began chanting "Cape Town, Cape Town".
The Western Cape provincial minister of sport, Lerumo Kalako, said he was convinced that Cape Town would win the 2004 games when the IOC announced its final decision in September.
"From now we are going to redouble our efforts to win the games," he said.
Ncgonde Balfour, a senior member of Cape Town's Olympic Bid Committee and former black activist said:
"I knew deep down in my heart, I knew. In September we will win, and in 2004, we will present the most unique, the most magnificent, the most wonderful African games."
